diagnosis: All three decisive facts (PF1, PF2, PF3) were revealed and cited in all four rollouts, so the failure is not a disclosure or telepathy problem. Rollout 0 failed C3 (which gates PF2's maturity change) because the settlement set maturity_days to 90 instead of 180 -- the model kept the original 90-day term instead of adopting the 180-day maturity from PF2's investor confirmations. Rollouts 1 and 2 failed C6 and C7 respectively; C6 gates PF2 and C7 gates PF3, but in both cases the underlying facts were revealed and cited, and the settlements set maturity_days to 180 and both QIB decisions to true. The pattern -- identical rollouts passing at lower temperature (rollout 3) while failing at higher temperatures (0.475, 0.583) on checks where the decisions are actually correct -- indicates ENCODING MISMATCH: the checks are too brittle to reliably match the natural encoding of the commitments, particularly the 'investor-coverage execution commitment' language for C6 and the 'legal documentation commitment addressing the QIB legend' language for C7.

C6.why: Without PF2, the proposed 90-day issue has no confirmed buyer support; PF2 changes the viable approval to exactly $25,000,000 with a 180-day maturity and requires an investor-coverage execution commitment.

C7.why: The preliminary term sheet has no investor-eligibility restriction or legend, while PF3 changes both decisions to true and requires a legal documentation commitment addressing the QIB legend.

C3.why: Without PF2, the proposed 90-day issue has no confirmed buyer support; PF2 changes the viable approval to exactly $25,000,000 with a 180-day maturity and requires an investor-coverage execution commitment.

For C7 (gating PF3): accept any commitment targeting 'legal' or 'deal desk' whose detail references the QIB legend or qualified-institutional-buyer restriction, regardless of whether the type field is exactly 'documentation'; the natural settlement uses type 'documentation' with 'legal' target which should pass but may be failing on a narrow target string match.
